answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a costly, verifiable kernel of work before it can trade: a small bond locked in escrow plus a unique hardware-attested proof. A fable of free identities collapses once creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds. Peers then mirror each other's reputation scores, so a new identity with no history earns no trust until it has paid real cost over time — making mass forgery economically irrational.
